methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $5.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Rapidus is a late-stage semiconductor company that has raised $5.0B+ to date. The comparable universe in Chips & Semiconductors spans 11 total peers—3 public (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private entities including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent—though none align sufficiently on stage and valuation tier to support reliable peer-median pricing.

Given data constraints, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised ($5.0B) as a baseline value proxy for a late-stage enterprise, a 1.2x step-up multiplier—standard for progression toward series maturity—yields $6.0B. This reflects the typical capital efficiency and risk reduction embedded in late-stage advancement within semiconductor development.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $5.1B to $6.9B, with a median estimate of $6.0B. Material uncertainty remains around comparable-stage precedent in the narrow semiconductor frontier-tech category; the single-method foundation means sensitivity to assumptions about appropriate step-up multiples and the representativeness of total raised as a valuation anchor. Market conditions, clinical or technical validation milestones, and capital deployment velocity will be primary drivers of refinement.
